samples.question: The picture is a wide instrument sheet. Along its extreme left edge and along its extreme right edge there is one vertical column of horizontal bars, and the wide corridor between the two columns holds only decoration. Exactly two bars in the whole picture are coloured: one red bar and one blue bar. They are the calibration bars, they always lie in opposite columns - one on the left, one on the right - and either of them may be the longer one. Call the length of the shorter calibration bar the low mark and the length of the longer calibration bar the high mark; both are lengths, not positions. Every pure black bar, in either column, is a measurement bar. All grey and pale grey marks anywhere in the picture - bars, plates and tick lattices, inside the columns as well as in the corridor - are decoration and are never counted. Only a bar's length matters; its column, its height on the sheet, its left end and the order of the bars do not. No measurement bar ever has exactly the length of a calibration bar. Counting the measurement bars of both columns together, how many pure black bars are strictly longer than the low mark and strictly shorter than the high mark? Answer with a single whole number.
